claim: For an HMM hidden-state cap R, populations probabilities through length 2R-1 suffice to reveal a complete predictive Hankel basis. Raw-trajectory estimators can recover unknown observable rank and a finite realization under explicit singular-gap and, for CUR, coherence/conditioning assumptions.
interface: Raw observed prefixes from independent episodes or an explicitly mixing single stream; no entry oracle or supplied basis. The exact sampling interface differs by leaf and must not be merged.
cost_and_baseline: Word tables can be exponential in R; sample counts depend on the explicit gap/mass/conditioning terms. Full raw-data baselines see all prefix indicators and can simulate CUR selection; no trajectory-sample advantage is proved.
open_gate: Rank-free task-risk certification without a singular gap, and stable positive-HMM realization at finite precision, remain UNKNOWN.

claim: For the stationary symmetric binary HMM with both unknown transition and emission parameters lambda,m in [1/2,3/4], two raw lag moments from one path give worst-history one-step TV O(T^-1/2), one-step KL O(T^-1), and H-step future KL O(H/T); a full-path Le Cam pair matches the one-step TV and KL rates.
interface: One stationary raw observation path, unknown transition and emission parameters, no hidden labels or conditional-query interface.
cost_and_baseline: T symbols, one initial stationary start, O(T) streaming work, O(log T) moment counters, two parameter outputs. The full-path lower bound applies to the strongest same-data learner.
open_gate: This is a structured two-state class with fixed margins. Generic-HMM dependence and filter-stability transfer remain UNKNOWN; no matching lower in growing H is proved.

claim: A K-state/K^2-parameter fast-mixing family has expected one-context TV minimax risk of order min(1,K/sqrt(N)); the full-support HMM version has context mass, transition/emission floors, and unnormalized pair-block singular scale explicitly shrinking as 1/K.
interface: One stationary raw path of n observations; no hidden labels. The noisy HMM endpoint forecasts after one observed symbol; the deterministic endpoint is a finite-state Markov source whose one-symbol context is sufficient for the whole past.
cost_and_baseline: The empirical pair-law upper and Assouad lower both use the full raw path. A single bit affects two transition rows; the proof sums over K^2/4 directions.
open_gate: No general arbitrary-HMM or multi-step joint-KL minimax theorem follows; novelty and external review remain UNKNOWN.

claim: An unknown sparse predictive dictionary can be recovered from raw trajectories of a fully observable Markov chain under pure-anchor, convex-hull, coverage, mixing, and coefficient-gap promises.
interface: One raw observable-state stream; no supplied feature dictionary, row query, or intervention.
cost_and_baseline: Counts and mixing gaps are explicit; retained full trajectories are at least as informed. No information-theoretic sample advantage is claimed.
open_gate: Extension to hidden-state HMMs and removal of anchor/separation promises remain UNKNOWN.

claim: Several explicit controlled-HMM tasks exhibit finite-sample feedback advantages over matched precommitted schedules, and complete action-prefix support through 2K-1 identifies the minimal interventional Hankel realization up to similarity.
interface: Legal actions and raw observations only. The examples have known restricted model families or known kernels; the causal result supplies exhaustive support and a state cap.
cost_and_baseline: The named risk and action/reset costs are matched. Complete action-prefix schedules are exponential in the state cap. Two cue-alignment examples share a mechanism and are not counted as independent general evidence.
open_gate: Adaptive unknown-basis acquisition for general HMMs remains UNKNOWN.

claim: Any basis-selection or CUR procedure that is a function of the observed raw trajectories can be simulated by an equally informed strategy retaining those trajectories; possible wins are in priced storage or arithmetic, not statistical information under this interface.
interface: Same raw observations and task stream; retaining strategy may compute and cache derived state.
cost_and_baseline: Exact information and risk simulation; storage and computation remain separate explicit resources.
open_gate: A net advantage under a specified storage/runtime budget against the strongest retainer remains UNKNOWN.
